body:
Queue-head preparation and position admission currently depend on one another for carrier selection and source caching. Move the existing pure carrier selector to the position policy owner so queue-head preparation can use it directly. Keep `position_queue_admission.select_carrier` as the same compatibility export and leave the source cache and writer fences unchanged.

The selector's AST matches the original. The selected interface guard passes. Focused position admission, introduction and queue-head checks passed 26 tests, with 2 skipped; two additional fixture tests fail identically on the untouched base because their `object()` database fake does not implement the current Study timezone fence:

- `test_refresh_consumes_prepared_due_before_advancing`
- `test_all_covered_ordinary_introduction_is_skipped_without_completion`

Registry ownership and dependency mapping are coordinated separately. Native position introduction and issued-head/replay checks and the assembled saved-review to playable-next journey have not run on this head. No installation or activation is claimed.

## Summary by Sourcery

Extract the shared position carrier policy so queue-head preparation and position admission use a single owner without changing their existing behavior.

Enhancements:
- Centralize pure position carrier selection under the position-learning policy owner while preserving the existing admission-module export for compatibility.
- Allow queue-head preparation and position admission to share the carrier policy without changing source-cache or writer-fence behavior.

Documentation:
- Document the shared carrier policy and clarify that source caching remains owned by queue-head preparation.

Tests:
- Verify that the legacy admission export references the shared carrier policy and update queue-head timing coverage to patch the new owner.
title: Extract shared position carrier policy
head: codex/position-carrier-policy
